metadata.title: A real-complement modulus implication for compact subsets of the line
metadata.description:
For every compact E contained in[0,1], let F be its complement within the real line and let S2 be the circle of radius2. We prove that positive planar2-modulus of all curves joining E to S2 forces infinite2-modulus of all curves joining E to F. This answers the explicit implication in the2018 version of Hayman-Lingham Problem7.58, including compact sets of zero length and positive capacity. The proof constructs actual boundary values from a pointwise weighted metric, uses critical trace rigidity to force zero length under finite target energy, and then derives a contradiction by small circular connectors. Both global rectifiability and the stated local-off-endpoints convention are treated.

Classical foundations and independently checked audit-composed deductions from older general theory are acknowledged. No claim of firstness, a new mechanism, an earlier explicitly printed resolution, or current worldwide openness is made. Priority searches are bounded; full2019 wording and an1982 talk body remain unauthenticated. The deposit contains the preprint and a portable TeX-source, written-proof, independent-reconstruction, integrity-verification and priority-audit archive. AI tools were used extensively in research, proof development, literature review, internal adversarial verification and writing. This preprint is unrefereed; no external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.
